flashcards.q: State the mean-variance optimization problem and the closed form for GMV weights.
flashcards.a: min w'Sigma w s.t. mu'w = r_target, 1'w = 1. GMV ignores mu: w = Sigma^-1 1 / (1'Sigma^-1 1). Tangency: w proportional to Sigma^-1 (mu - rf).

flashcards.q: Why is unconstrained MVO called an 'error maximizer'?
flashcards.a: It loads on assets whose measured means were luckily high and vols luckily low. Sigma^-1 amplifies estimation error exactly where data is weakest; corner solutions reverse out-of-sample (Jobson-Korkie 1981; Michaud 1989).
E[Ri] = Rf + beta_i (E[Rm] - Rf) with beta_i = Cov(Ri,Rm)/Var(Rm). Only covariance with the market is priced; idiosyncratic risk diversifies away free and earns zero premium.

flashcards.q: Why is the empirical security market line flatter than theory predicts?
flashcards.a: Leverage-constrained investors reach for return by buying high-beta stocks instead of borrowing, depressing high-beta expected returns (Black's zero-beta model 1972; Frazzini-Pedersen BAB 2014 across ~90 years and ~19 markets).
The true market portfolio includes all wealth (human capital, property) and is unobservable, so CAPM tests are joint tests of the proxy. A rejection may reflect proxy error, not theory failure.

flashcards.q: List the five Fama-French factors plus Carhart's addition, with rough historical premia.
flashcards.a: MKT, SMB (~2-4%/yr), HML (~2-4%/yr), RMW profitability, CMA investment (FF5, 2015); UMD momentum (Carhart 1997) historically strongest gross long-short premium but crash-prone (Jan-Mar 2009 drawdown region ~70%, worst single month ~ -49%).

flashcards.q: What hurdle did Harvey-Liu-Zhu propose for new factor claims and why?
flashcards.a: t-statistic > 3.0 instead of 2.0: with 316+ published factors tested, conventional thresholds produce too many false discoveries; post-publication decay shrinks most premia further.

flashcards.q: Derive ERC weights for two assets.
flashcards.a: Equalize RC_i = w_i(Sigma w)_i / sigma_p^2. For N=2 correlation drops out: w1 = sigma2/(sigma1+sigma2), w2 = sigma1/(sigma1+sigma2). For N>=3 no closed form; iterate w_i proportional to 1/(Sigma w)_i or solve log-barrier system.

flashcards.q: What fraction of 60/40 risk comes from equities, and what does risk parity do about it?
flashcards.a: Roughly 90-95% (16% vol vs 5% vol at corr ~0.2). Risk parity equalizes contributions, tilting capital toward bonds and levering ~2-3x to hit a ~10% fund vol target.

flashcards.q: How big is the standard error on a 60-month sample mean of a 16%-vol asset?
flashcards.a: SE = sigma/sqrt(T) annualized: 0.16/sqrt(5) ~= 7.2% per-month-window... properly: monthly sigma ~4.62%/sqrt(60) -> ~0.6%/mo -> ~2.3%/yr. Compare to equity risk premium ~4-6%: your estimate error rivals the signal.

flashcards.q: What does Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage do and typical intensities?
flashcards.a: Blends sample covariance toward a structured target (constant-correlation/identity-scaled) minimizing Frobenius loss; typical shrinkage intensity 10-40%. Stabilizes inversion when N approaches T.

flashcards.q: What happened to balanced portfolios in 2022 and which assumption broke?
flashcards.a: Stocks ~-18% total return, Bloomberg US Agg ~-13% (worst bond year on record), stock-bond correlation flipped positive under inflation shock. Broke the negative-correlation ballast assumption behind RP leverage, LDI, and 60/40; RP drew down ~20-30%.
